l1.text: Ever read the same sentence three times and still have no idea what it said?

l2.text: That feeling is often called brain fog—and it's a common complaint after a concussion.

l3.text: It can feel like your thoughts are slower, your memory isn't as sharp, or it takes more effort to concentrate.

l4.text: And brain fog isn't the same thing as being lazy or simply not trying hard enough.

l5.text: After a concussion, the brain may have a harder time efficiently processing and coordinating information. Tasks that used to feel automatic can suddenly require much more effort.

l6.text: That's why a busy day can sometimes leave you feeling completely drained—even when you haven't done anything physically demanding.

l7.text: If brain fog is getting in the way of your day, don't just push through it. Your brain may need the right evaluation and recovery plan.
